THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:

JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 20.04.2018 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Vijayapura (for short 'tribunal') in MVC no.26/2016, this appeal is filed.
2. Shri.
Sanganagouda
V. Biradar, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that since insurer had not preferred appeal against award, finding of Tribunal regarding occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle due to its rash and negligent driving and claimant sustaining injuries in said accident is not in dispute.
Issuance of insurance policy and its coverage as on date of accident are also not in dispute.
It was submitted that as on date of accident i.e., 02.08.2015, claimant was 34 years of age, earning NC: 2023:KHC-K:7390 Rs.10,000/- per month from agriculture.
Claimant sustained Grade III-B fracture of distal of left femur and first metatarsal Pharyngeal joint with Calcaneum assessed by PW.2-doctor to have caused 45% disability to limb.
However, tribunal considered only 18% towards functional disability and awarded inadequate compensation.

It was submitted that since claimant had sustained Grade III-B fracture of femur, apart from fracture of metatarsal and calcaneum,
award of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering would be inadequate.
Therefore, sought enhancement compensation under specific heads i.e., 'future loss of income' and towards 'pain and suffering'.
3. On other hand, Shri Subhash Mallapur, learned counsel for respondent no.2-insurer sought to justify award.
4. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award.

2 NC: 2023:KHC-K:7390 5.

From above submission and since only claimant was in appeal for enhancement of compensation,
point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
6.

From medical treatment records namely, Wound Certificate, Medical Bills, Photos, Disability Certificate, Medical Certificate, Discharge Summary, X-ray Films, Case Sheet and MLC information copy, marked as Exs.P5, P8 to P16 respectively, it is seen that claimant has sustained Grade III-B fracture of left distal of femur, fracture of first metatarsal Pharyngeal joint and fracture of left calcaneum.
Two of these fractures would be grievous.
Therefore, award of Rs.50,000/- towards pain and suffering would be inadequate.

Same is enhanced to Rs.75,000/-.
7.
As per Ex.P11, Dr.Shekhar examined as PW.2 has stated that said fractures resulted in disability of 45% to limb.
However, as noted by tribunal, there is no NC: 2023:KHC-K:7390 assessment of loss of earning capacity by PW.2.

Since PW.2 noted shortening of left leg by 4 cms. and restriction of movement of left leg beyond 900, apart from observing that claimant required walking stick,
assessment of functional disability at 18% would be inadequate.

It would be appropriate to enhance it to '25%'.
8.
Insofar as monthly income, though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month from agriculture, same is not substantiated.
Hence, same has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2015 is Rs.8,000/- and same has to be considered as monthly income of claimant.
Claimant was 36 years of age as on date of accident.
Hence multiplier applicable would be '15'.

Thus,
compensation towards 'future loss of income' would be:
Rs.8,000 x 25% x 12 x 15 = Rs.3,60,000/-.
9.

Compensation awarded under other heads namely, attendant and other incidental expenses, loss of NC: 2023:KHC-K:7390 income during laid up period, loss of amenities and unhappiness in life,
medical expenses and future medical expenses would appear to be just and proper and do not call for enhancement.
10. Thus, total compensation would be Rs.7,18,651/-.
Tribunal has awarded total compensation of Rs.5,60,000/-.
Thereby, there is enhancement by Rs.1,58,651/-.
11. Point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. Claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,58,651/- with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit.
iii. Respondent no.2-insurer is directed to deposit same within six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
